quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: An emergency vehicle is approaching with its siren and flashing lights while you are crossing an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.
Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Finish crossing the intersection, then pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or a siren, finish crossing the intersection first. Then drive to the right and stop. You must yield to police cars, fire trucks, ambulances, and other emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: When parking on a hill, what should you do?

options.text: One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.
Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
Your front wheels should be parallel to the road if there is no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.
questions.explanation: Always use your parking brake and leave your vehicle in park when parking on a hill. If there is no curb, turn your front wheels away from the center of the road so the vehicle will roll safely if the brakes fail. If there is a curb, turn your wheels toward it when going downhill, or away from it when going uphill.

questions.question: When using windshield wipers in rain, snow, or sleet, what else should you do?

options.text: Honk your horn to alert other drivers to the poor visibility.
Use your high beam headlights.
Use your low beam headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: You must turn on your low beam headlights when using windshield wipers due to weather. This helps other drivers see you. You do not need headlights if your wipers are only used occasionally.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Pedestrian crossing.
School crossing.
Jogging trail.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pedestrian crossing.
questions.explanation: This yellow and black warning sign tells drivers to watch for pedestrians crossing the road. Be alert and ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should never:

options.text: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.
Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cross the centerline in an intersection.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your blind spot and look for other drivers in the same lane. Never try to pass or change lanes inside an intersection.

questions.question: You have a green light, but the intersection is blocked by other traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Turn left and find another route.
Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
Follow other vehicles and enter the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.
questions.explanation: Even with a green light, do not enter the intersection if traffic is blocking it. If you get stuck in the intersection when the light turns red, you will block other traffic and may get a ticket.

questions.question: You are driving defensively when you:

options.text: Keep one car length between you and the car ahead.
Look only at the car directly in front of you.
Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Defensive driving means scanning ahead for potential hazards. Do not stare only at the road in front of your car. Look ahead and around your vehicle to spot dangers early.

questions.question: You exit the freeway on a downhill ramp that curves. What should you do?

options.text: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
Slow to the posted freeway speed limit.
Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow to a safe speed before the curve.
questions.explanation: Always slow down before entering a curve. You may not see hazards ahead, and braking in a curve can cause your vehicle to skid.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Do not proceed until the light turns green.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means stop completely. Come to a full stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians before proceeding.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
Follow other vehicles closely for better traction.
Pump your brakes to keep them from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a low gear before going down steep hills.
questions.explanation: Shift to a low gear before going downhill on slippery surfaces to prevent skidding. Keep more distance between you and the car ahead. Avoid quick stops. Pump your brakes if you do not have antilock brakes.

questions.question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, which lights should you use?

options.text: Low beams.
High beams.
Fog lights only.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, and snow. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare that makes it harder to see.

questions.question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?

options.text: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing.
Because following closely will trap you in the vehicle's slipstream.

questions.correctAnswerText: To see around the sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles block your view of the road. The driver may not be able to see you directly behind them. Increase your distance so you can see around the vehicle and see the road ahead.

questions.question: When making a left turn from a one-way street, which lane should you be in?

options.text: The lane nearest the left curb.
The lane nearest the center of the street.
The lane nearest the right curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane nearest the left curb.
questions.explanation: Always turn from the lane closest to the direction you are turning. For a left turn from a one-way street, use the lane nearest the left curb.

questions.question: When turning left from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?

options.text: Near the right-hand side of the road.
Near the centerline.
On the left of the centerline.

questions.correctAnswerText: Near the centerline.
questions.explanation: Position your vehicle near the centerline when preparing to turn left from a two-way street. Begin your turn just before reaching the center of the intersection. Turn into the first available legal lane without cutting the corner.

questions.question: What does a dashed yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A dashed line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection?

options.text: Yield to all traffic before crossing.
Stop, then enter when it is safe.
Slow down and cross carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light tells drivers to slow down to a safe speed and proceed with caution.

questions.question: Traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make room for the merging traffic if possible.
Speed up to assert your right-of-way.
Always maintain your current position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for the merging traffic if possible.
questions.explanation: When it is safe, make room to allow vehicles to merge into your lane.

questions.question: How many points on your license within two years will result in a one-year suspension?

options.text: 18 to 20 points
21 to 23 points
24 or more points

questions.correctAnswerText: 24 or more points
questions.explanation: If you get 24 or more points within two years, your license will be suspended for 365 days.

questions.question: Before backing your vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Walk around the entire vehicle to check for people or objects behind it.
Look at the front, sides, and rear.
Do both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do both of the above.
questions.explanation: Walk around your vehicle to make sure no people or objects are behind it. Then look to the front, sides, and rear. While backing, look over your right shoulder toward the rear. Do not rely only on mirrors.

questions.question: Which statement about medications and driving is true?

options.text: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
Over-the-counter medications cannot affect your driving if taken as directed.
Medications prescribed by a doctor are always safe to take while driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.
questions.explanation: Both prescription and over-the-counter medications can impair your driving. Cold and allergy medicines can cause drowsiness. It is your responsibility to know how any medication affects your ability to drive.

questions.question: When is a U-turn not allowed?

options.text: In a parking lot.
On or near a curve or hill.
On a straight road with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: On or near a curve or hill.
questions.explanation: Never turn around on or near a curve or hill. You cannot see oncoming traffic or pedestrians. This can cause a crash.

questions.question: When should you give up your right-of-way?

options.text: Often, even at controlled intersections.
Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
Never. It confuses other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Whenever it helps prevent crashes.
questions.explanation: Do not assume other drivers will give you the right-of-way. Give up your right-of-way whenever it helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver does not dim their headlights, where should you look?

options.text: Toward the center of the road.
Toward the right side of the road.
Straight ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded by the bright headlights and helps you see the road. Do not use your bright lights to retaliate.

questions.question: Driving slower than other traffic is:

options.text: A good idea if the weather is bad.
OK if you do not know the speed limit.
Often dangerous because frustrated drivers may try to pass you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Often dangerous because frustrated drivers may try to pass you.
questions.explanation: Driving slower than other traffic is dangerous. Drivers behind you may get impatient and take risky chances to pass you.

questions.question: When you see a green arrow, you must:

options.text: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
Yield to pedestrians only.
Wait four seconds before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means "go." Turn in the direction of the arrow after you yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians still in the intersection.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. You can only turn left onto another one-way street if:

options.text: You speed up before the turn.
Traffic on that street moves to the right.
Traffic on that street moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic on that street moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves left if there is no sign prohibiting it. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves right.

questions.question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on an interstate, you should:

options.text: Change lanes to the left.
Slow down.
Keep your speed and position the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes to the left.
questions.explanation: Watch for upcoming on-ramps. When traffic allows, move to the left lane to give vehicles room to enter from the on-ramps.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing ahead.
questions.explanation: A round sign always means a railroad crossing is ahead.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck driver to stop.
Other drivers when they slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck driver to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks take longer to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic light means you may:

options.text: Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.
Not turn until the light turns green.
Turn in that direction after a complete stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not turn until the light turns green.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means "stop." Stay stopped until a green light or green arrow appears. Do not turn against a red arrow.

questions.question: If you cannot find a gap to enter the freeway, you should:

options.text: Maintain your speed and force other drivers to create a gap.
Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
Stop at the end of the ramp to wait for a gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap.
questions.explanation: Slow down on the ramp to wait for a gap. Do not stop at the end of the ramp or you will not have enough space to speed up before entering the road.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Road changes direction or narrows.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road changes direction or narrows.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a change in direction or a narrowing road. You may see several of these signs on sharp curves or near narrow bridges.

questions.question: You are in a left turn lane at an intersection with oncoming traffic. You should:

options.text: Move to the left of the center lane.
Signal about 100 feet before the intersection.
Turn your front wheels left to prepare for the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal about 100 feet before the intersection.
questions.explanation: Signal about 100 feet before turning left. Keep your front wheels straight until it is safe to turn. This protects you if another car hits you from behind.

questions.question: A vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you. What should you do first?

options.text: Honk and brake hard.
Release the gas pedal.
Swerve into the next lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: If a vehicle pulls in front of you too close, take your foot off the gas pedal. This creates space between you and the other vehicle without slamming on the brakes or swerving.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Road construction or maintenance ahead.
Side road.
Railroad ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road construction or maintenance ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn of hazards. Orange diamond signs warn of construction or maintenance areas.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped sign means:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
Warning.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning.
questions.explanation: A yellow diamond sign warns of possible danger ahead. Orange diamond signs warn of dangers in or near work areas.

questions.question: If you are about to be hit from behind, you should NOT:

options.text: Apply your brakes.
Let go of the steering wheel.
Press your head against the head restraint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let go of the steering wheel.
questions.explanation: Press yourself against the back of your seat and put your head against the head restraint to prevent whiplash. Hold the steering wheel firmly and be ready to brake to avoid hitting the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: When entering a freeway, check traffic by:

options.text: Using your rearview and side mirrors.
Using your rearview mirror.
Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: When entering any roadway, use your side mirror and look over your shoulder. This helps you see traffic and know when it is safe to merge.

questions.question: You should give extra space when following:

options.text: A station wagon.
A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
A small passenger car.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver who cannot see behind their vehicle.
questions.explanation: Drivers of trucks, buses, vans, or vehicles pulling trailers may not see you behind them. Increase your following distance. Large vehicles can also block your view of the road, so stay back to see around them.

questions.question: The light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. You should:

options.text: Slow down and proceed through without caution.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means "caution" and the light will turn red soon. Stop if you can do so safely. Otherwise, cross carefully.
